title: Chapter 4 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Dynamic Routes & API Routes!

questions.question: Which file naming pattern creates a dynamic segment in Next.js?
questions.explanation: Square brackets define dynamic segments. `[id].js` matches any value in that position.

questions.question: How do you access the dynamic route parameter on the client side?
questions.explanation: The `useRouter` hook provides `router.query` which contains the dynamic segments.

questions.question: `router.query` is always an empty object during pre‑rendering.
questions.explanation: On the server (in `getStaticProps`/`getServerSideProps`), you must use `context.params` because `router` is not available.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `getStaticPaths` for a dynamic page?
options: To define which dynamic instances are pre‑rendered at build time
To fetch data for the page
questions.explanation: `getStaticPaths` lists all the paths that should be statically generated for a dynamic page.

questions.question: What does the file `pages/blog/[...slug].js` match?
questions.explanation: The catch‑all `[...slug]` matches one or more segments. It does not match the exact parent path `/blog`.

questions.question: In a catch‑all route `pages/docs/[...params].js`, what is the value of `router.query.params` for `/docs/nextjs/routing`?
questions.explanation: Catch‑all parameters are always an array of path segments.

questions.question: To make a catch‑all route match the parent path as well, use double brackets: `[[...slug]].js`. This type is called ______ catch‑all.
questions.explanation: Optional catch‑all routes handle zero segments as well.

questions.question: How do you represent the root path of an optional catch‑all in `getStaticPaths`?
questions.explanation: An empty array signals no segments (i.e., the base path).

questions.question: Where are API routes located in a Next.js project?
questions.explanation: Files inside `pages/api` are treated as serverless API endpoints.

questions.question: API route handlers receive `req` and `res` objects identical to Express.
questions.explanation: They are standard Node.js `http.IncomingMessage` and `http.ServerResponse` with some added helpers, but not Express objects.

questions.question: How do you send a JSON response from an API route?
questions.explanation: Next.js extends `res` with a `.json()` method for convenience.

questions.question: How do you access query string parameters in an API route?
questions.explanation: Next.js automatically parses the query string and populates `req.query`.

questions.question: `req.body` is automatically parsed and available in all API routes.
questions.explanation: Body parsing is not built‑in; you need to handle the stream manually or use a library.

questions.question: Which HTTP method check is correct inside an API handler?
questions.explanation: Use `req.method` to determine the HTTP verb.

questions.question: What is the advantage of using SWR over manual `useEffect` + `fetch` for API routes?
options: It makes the code run on the server
It provides caching, automatic revalidation, and simpler state management
It works only with static pages
questions.explanation: SWR abstracts away loading/error states, caches, and revalidates in the background.

questions.question: To call an API route from the browser, you can use a relative URL like `______`. (example path)
questions.explanation: Since the API is served from the same origin, relative paths like `/api/hello` work.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to build an API route that returns a list of posts at `GET /api/posts`?
options: Create `pages/api/posts.js` and export a default handler
API routes only support dynamic files
questions.explanation: Like pages, both `posts.js` and `posts/index.js` map to `/api/posts`.

questions.question: You can use dynamic segments in API routes, like `pages/api/posts/[id].js`.
questions.explanation: API routes support the same file‑system routing, including dynamic segments.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of having API routes in the same project as your frontend?
options: You can deploy both frontend and backend together as a single unit
It forces you to use TypeScript
It eliminates the need for databases
questions.explanation: API routes allow you to build a full‑stack application within one codebase and deploy it seamlessly.

questions.question: When calling an API route from `getStaticProps`, what URL format should you use?
options: You cannot call API routes from `getStaticProps`
questions.explanation: On the server, there is no browser origin, so you need an absolute URL. In development, use `http://localhost:3000`; in production, use the deployed domain or an environment variable.
